basis: Severe ulceronecrotic PLEVA directly destroys skin; secondary ulcer infection does not establish a defining infectious disease.
Limb/jaw defects and microstomia define syndrome; renal hypoplasia/insufficiency and ID each 30-79%; hearing loss and myopia omitted by cap.
Clonal blood-cell glycosylation defect exposes Tn antigen, producing antibody-mediated polyagglutination. [Study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16251947/)
Short ribs, thoracic and pelvic dysplasia, and laryngeal stenosis are defining structural abnormalities.
Hamartomatous cysts, renal dysplasia and lung fibrosis define the disease; secondary renal hypertension is a separately diagnosed consequence.
NK/T lymphocyte lymphoma typically originates in nasal/sinonasal or upper airway tissue; distant spread and orbital invasion are not universal.
Dicarboxylate transport/metabolic disorder with leukoencephalopathy and neurologic dysfunction; abnormal urinary metabolites do not establish kidney damage.
Site-variable tumour umbrella; CNS and lung are explicitly listed origins; mediastinal and retroperitoneal sites lack a dedicated axis.
Pontocerebellar degeneration and congenital contractures define PCH4; central apnea and neurogenic dysphagia do not establish lung or gut damage.
ASNS metabolic encephalopathy; visual loss is mainly cortical; optic hypoplasia lacks a reliable >=30% frequency. [GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK525916/)
Neoplasms of hematopoietic histiocytes/dendritic cells; no extranodal organ or immune-mediated disorder is shared across this umbrella.
Neoplasm originates in the ear; the umbrella does not require a skin or nervous-system origin.
Plasmodium infects erythrocytes, with cerebral sequestration and encephalopathy defining this malaria subtype.
Inherited disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis is a keratinization disorder confined to skin.
Defective steroidogenesis causes adrenal dysfunction; defining skeletal malformations occur in 80-99%; genital abnormalities add no reproductive axis.
Dural venous thrombosis; persistent cranial neuropathies ~50%, visual impairment <20%. [Review](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK448177/)
Cardiovascular laterality/heterotaxy concept; reversed abdominal organ position alone does not demonstrate hepatic or gastrointestinal damage.
Congenital reversal of the great arterial connections is a structural cardiovascular defect.
Neuroendocrine tumour originates in gastric mucosa; neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish endocrine-gland disease.
Childhood neoplasm of the testis is a reproductive-site tumour; endocrine dysfunction is not inherent to this umbrella.
Congenital abdominal-wall fascial defect; cryptorchidism has no axis. [Orphanet](https://www.orpha.net/en/disease/detail/314432)
Aniridia/lens dislocation, intellectual disability and abnormal upper incisors define the syndrome; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with spastic paraplegia; micrognathia 4/8 and fixed finger contractures 2/2 support skeletal involvement; eye/ear findings isolated.
Benign multiple intraductal breast papillomas; breast has no axis. [NCI/MedGen](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/medgen/235123)
Platelet defect and oculocutaneous albinism; lung fibrosis in most adults; colitis variable/cap. [GeneReviews](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1287/)
